system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the atom, answer "hold" for that check and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure between pass and a non-pass value, choose the non-pass value and explain.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom. pass = fully stated. revise = the core claim is stated, and the gap is only wording, strength, or a dropped/extra peripheral qualifier that can be fixed by deleting or softening words (say what). fail = not stated, OR the atom adds substantive content the evidence lacks: a scope or population restriction (e.g. 'In B-ALL'), a mechanism or operation, a characterization (e.g. 'an unbounded while loop'), or a formula/definition. If deleting the unsupported part would change what the atom tests, it is fail, not revise. For pass, put the supporting evidence ids in cite (required).
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / revise / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge: one fact a person who studied the concept would simply know. revise = the core fact is recall-level but the sentence carries extra load that must be removed, e.g. stacked conditions (since/although/if ... and ...), a procedural or evaluative add-on ('easy to define but requires checking ...'), or a clause that introduces a second technical concept that must be known separately (e.g. 'if X is an inner Kan complex' when that is not the card concept). fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = the authors' opinion or choice, or the finding of one study, so the answer is not fixed without the source.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a single system, product, or one study's topic.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Forward progress guarantees
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Covers what the book says about work-items, sub-groups and work-groups lacking guaranteed forward progress, how this affects barriers, cross-work-group synchronization and the device-wide latch, and the contrast with CUDA independent thread scheduling. Excludes formal progress-model theory not in the text.

ATOMS:
- DPCPP2-C02-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: In SYCL basic data-parallel kernels, the execution model allows completely parallel execution of work-items but neither guarantees nor requires it, so items may run in any order, including sequentially on a single hardware thread.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0136-s03] allows for completely parallel execution but does not guarantee or require it.
    [DPCPP2-p0136-s04] Items can be executed in any order, including sequentially on a single hardware thread (i.e., without any parallelism)!
- DPCPP2-C02-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: Work-items within a work-group are scheduled so that they can cooperate, but they are not required to provide any specific forward progress guarantees, and executing them sequentially between barriers and collectives is a valid implementation.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0146-s10] Second, although the work-items in a work-group are scheduled
    [DPCPP2-p0146-s11] such that they can cooperate with one another, they are not required to provide any specific forward progress guarantees—executing the work-items within a work-group sequentially between barriers and collectives is a valid implementation.
- DPCPP2-C02-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: Work-items within a sub-group are not required to provide any specific forward progress guarantees, so an implementation may execute each work-item sequentially and switch between work-items only when a sub-group collective function is encountered.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0148-s10] Like work-groups, the work-items in a sub-group are not required to
    [DPCPP2-p0148-s11] provide any specific forward progress guarantees—an implementation is free to execute each work-item in a sub-group sequentially and only switch between work-items when a sub-group collective function is encountered.
- DPCPP2-C02-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: Communication and synchronization between work-items in the same work-group is guaranteed to be safe only when performed using the provided barrier and collective functions, and hand-coded synchronization routines may deadlock.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0146-s12] Communication and synchronization between work-items in the same work-group is only guaranteed to be safe when performed using the barrier and collective functions provided, and hand-coded synchronization routines may deadlock.
- DPCPP2-C02-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: A device-wide latch built on atomics requires that the device be able to execute all work-groups in the ND-range simultaneously with strong forward progress guarantees, so that the elected leaders of every work-group eventually reach the latch.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0574-s07] 3. The device must be capable of executing all work-
    [DPCPP2-p0574-s08] groups in the ND-­range simultaneously, with strong forward progress guarantees, in order to ensure that the elected leaders of every work-group in the NDrange eventually reach the latch.
- DPCPP2-C02-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: A device-wide latch built on atomics requires that the elected leader of each work-group make progress independently of the leaders in other work-groups, to avoid a single work-item spinning in the loop from starving other work-items that have yet to increment the counter.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0574-s05] 2. The elected leader of each work-group in the ND-
    [DPCPP2-p0574-s06] range must make progress independently of the leaders in other work-groups, to avoid a single work-item spinning in the loop from starving other work-items that have yet to increment the counter.
- DPCPP2-C02-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: CUDA devices with independent thread scheduling let individual threads make progress independently, so a syntactically correct SYCL program ported from CUDA may not execute correctly on all SYCL devices that lack such stronger forward progress guarantees.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0607-s05] For CUDA devices with independent thread scheduling, the individual
    [DPCPP2-p0607-s06] CUDA threads make progress independently, rather than as a group.
    [DPCPP2-p0607-s07] These additional forward progress guarantees enable code patterns to execute safely on a CUDA device that may not execute correctly on a SYCL device without the stronger forward progress guarantees.
- DPCPP2-C02-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: The memory ordering guarantees provided by atomics are orthogonal to forward progress guarantees, so relying on memory order alone to implement synchronization primitives may lead to deadlocks when forward progress guarantees are not sufficiently strong.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0573-s08] The memory ordering guarantees provided by atomics are orthogonal to forward progress guarantees, and, at the time of writing, work-group scheduling in SYCL is completely implementation-defined.
    [DPCPP2-p0574-s01] Relying on memory order alone to implement synchronization primitives may lead to deadlocks in the absence of sufficiently strong forward progress guarantees!
- DPCPP2-C02-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: On some devices all sub-groups within a work-group are guaranteed to eventually make progress, but this is currently implementation-defined behavior, so kernels that must remain portable cannot rely on sub-groups making progress.
  EVIDENCE:
    [DPCPP2-p0148-s12] However, on some devices, all sub-groups within a work-group are guaranteed to execute (make progress) eventually, which is a cornerstone
    [DPCPP2-p0149-s02] This is currently implementation-defined behavior, and so we cannot rely on sub-groups to make progress if we want our kernels to remain portable.
